# A ball times a limb, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_scale_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x a$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$:

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x a : x \in X \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_z = c_{z0} + c_{z1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X * a` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |
| `a * X` | `T`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |
| `X *= a` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c_x$ is normalized: $c_{x0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{x0} + c_{x1})$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $c_z$ is normalized: $c_{z0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{z0} + c_{z1})$.
- $\lvert (x a) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$.

The radius adds $U\,\lvert c_z\rvert + V$ for the rounding error of the center, where $U$ and $V$ are `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` of the center's kernel: its proved bound relative to the computed value, rounded up to `T`. Every step of the radius is rounded up.

| Center's kernel | $U$, $V$ for `double` | for `float` |
|---|---|---|
| [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md) | `0x1.0000000000001p-105`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.000002p-47f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_scale_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball.v), against `ball_scale_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_scale_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx0 cx1 rx a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec cx0 cx1 ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  0 <= rx ->
  let '(cz0, cz1, rz) := ball_scale_2 emin prec tie_even cx0 cx1 rx a in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  normalized_2 emin prec cz0 cz1 /\
  (forall x : R, Rabs (x - (cx0 + cx1)) <= rx -> Rabs ((x * a) - (cz0 + cz1)) <= rz).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius scaling (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_scale_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_scale_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md), [`rmul`](rmul.md), [`abs_upper_2`](abs_upper_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md).

```
# A ball with a 2-limb center times a number a of the format: the center by mul_2_1, plus
# U |cz| + V from the claims of mul_2_1.

(cz0, cz1) = mul_2_1(cx0, cx1, a)
aa         = abs(a)
t1         = rmul(aa, rx)
mz         = abs_upper_2(cz0, cz1)
d0         = rmul(const unit_computed(mul_2_1), mz)
d          = radd(d0, const tiny_computed(mul_2_1))
rz         = radd(t1, d)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_scale_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 52 062 280 | 0 | 1.26672 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 50 557 536 | 0 | 1.32283 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 842 866 | 0 | 1.375 (`fp:4:-4:1`) |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only `from_limbs_unchecked` or writing `limb[]` directly can make.
